chunks: And whatever is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, and from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil, and from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Aṭṭar, and from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with them - from Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Aṭṭar, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub. And I have also narrated it from my father and from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may Allah be pleased with them - from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the author's father who is a key narrator
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May Allah be pleased with them, a phrase of respect used for the narrators
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it, indicating direct transmission from the author
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, a prominent early Shia narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the authenticity of narrations from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of *al-istifdal* (proving by multiple independent chains) employed by Shaykh al-Saduq to authenticate the reliability of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, a key narrator in the Four Books. By citing his father and other prominent *rijal* figures, the text underscores the scholarly consensus on the trustworthiness of this specific transmission line within Twelver Shia hadith science.
